title: Quarter the optimizer batch (2^19 -> 2^17 tokens/step)
description: TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2**19 -> 2**17 and DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 128 -> 64, keeping grad_accum_steps = 1; nothing else changed.
reflection: val_bpb 0.992664 vs baseline 0.997359 (-0.0047). 3525 optimizer steps / 462M tokens vs the baseline's ~880 steps, at 37.1% MFU (down from ~40%: with only 131K tokens per step the Muon NS + AdamW call is a visible fraction of the 80ms step, and total tokens drop ~12%). So the batch really was far above critical batch size and step count is what was binding — the gain survives losing 12% of the tokens. Because a0/a1 both ran 2^18, the round now brackets the curve: if 2^18 lands between 0.9927 and 0.9974 the optimum is at or below 2^17 and 2^16 is worth one probe; if 2^18 beats 2^17 the optimum is in between and the sweep is done. Note the optimizer overhead is now the thing eating throughput at small batch, so a further halving has to beat a steeper MFU tax, and the step-indexed get_muon_momentum(step) 300-step ramp now completes 4x earlier in wall-clock than it was tuned for — an untested confound worth one cheap check later.
